name: Coupled Physics
description: A heat analysis and a stress analysis of the same geometry (both 2D or both 3D), solved together: the heat problem first, its temperature field handed to the stress problem (each analysis keeps its own mesh; every node of the stress mesh takes the temperature at its place in the heat mesh, nothing is extrapolated), then the stress problem with that temperature as a load of its own (thermal expansion coefficient and reference temperature come from the material). One Solve button, a combined result, the checks of the hand-over (nothing extrapolated, every point found, the average temperature kept, the stress solve used the field), a SELF-CHECK on stand-in analyses with known answers that prints PASS or FAIL beside the numbers, and a DIAGNOSTICS REPORT (also saved as diagnostics.txt in the project folder). It is a block of the Workbench: wire a 2D or 3D Thermal block and a 2D or 3D Static Structural block into its Physics cell. A 2D or 3D Fluid Flow analysis of the same geometry can be wired in as well: it exchanges heat with the solid (solved until the heat flux agrees on both sides), its wall pressure loads the stress analysis, and the structure can move the flow (steady, small displacements; in 3D the air mesh follows the body). The self-check also covers the fluid loops on stand-in analyses with known answers. In 2D the window holds the setups of all the analyses: a strip of buttons (Fluid, Thermal, Structural, Coupled, Viz) with marks, what one analysis hands to another shown as green locked rows in its Outline, and a Viz tab with the rendered result of the last solve (air temperature or pressure, the bent body, tracers, a playback, PNG and animation export; temperatures in degC). Only tried in a headless Qt, never seen on Windows. 3D analyses are not shown in the window yet (they keep their own tabs and Viz says so). Not yet: a stress that changes the temperature, buoyancy, a transient flow.
